title: Location Content Formats V1.5
description: Enumerates algorithmic/structural spatial content formats used to represent, partition, or index space in mapping and information services.

oneOf.description: Delaunay triangulation used for robust tessellation; dual of Voronoi; basis for many TIN implementations.
Thiessen/Voronoi cells partition space by nearest seed; widely used for influence/service areas and proximity regions.
Triangulated Irregular Network surface model (typically Delaunay-conforming) for elevation/terrain representation.

Public-domain hierarchical string geocode based on Z-order; compact keys with prefix locality for proximity search.
Quad-tree tile addressing (Bing/Slippy maps) where key length = zoom; encodes parent-child tile lineage.
Balanced MBR-based spatial index (and variants like R*-tree) used in databases (e.g., PostGIS GiST) for spatial queries.
Recursive 2D subdivision (NW/NE/SW/SE) used for rasters, imagery pyramids, and uneven point densities.
K-dimensional space-partitioning tree for nearest-neighbor and range queries on point sets.
